_about: The ONE contract of the runtimes list on the app ↔ web page bridge (`window.sprintableDesktop`, story 5009 · PO 11-25). The app's preload (mobile repo, desktop-electron/src/web-preload.ts) hands the page the programs it found; the web (apps/web/src/lib/desktop-app.ts) reads them. Both repos keep this file byte for byte the same and read the vectors below in their own tests — change one side and the vectors turn red. Why it exists: a web older than a program's name used to throw away the WHOLE bridge for one entry it did not know (the live dev walk lost the add-project folder field the day OpenCode was found), and an app must never be able to do that to a web of any age.

negotiation.rule: The bridge's `runtimes` property and a call without `accepts` carry ONLY the legacy names (what a web of any age knows). A page that names more in `accepts` also gets the names it asked for that the app knows. Names the app does not know add nothing; nothing valid asked = the legacy names. An app older than this contract ignores the second argument and sends what it always sent. A listener is called only when ITS visible list changed.

web_reads.rule: The web drops an entry whose runtime NAME it does not know — the bridge stays, that name is simply not shown (a name is never a refusal of the whole bridge). Everything else keeps its old strictness: an entry that is not an object, has no string `runtime`, or is a KNOWN name with a wrong shape (version · executable not strings) is not our app — the whole bridge is refused, as before.

web_vectors.name: only known names: the bridge is kept as it came
one name the web does not know, mixed in: the bridge is kept, that name is not shown
only an unknown name: the bridge is kept with an empty list
an unknown name with an odd shape is still just an unknown name
a known name with a wrong shape is not our app: the bridge is refused
an entry that is not an object: refused
an entry without a string runtime: refused
runtimes that is not a list: refused

app_vectors.name: no ask: legacy names only, OpenCode found or not
asks for opencode by name: gets it (and the legacy names)
asks for a name the app does not know: nothing more
asks with something that is not a list: legacy names only
